chapterTitle: Appendix B — Executable Invariant and Witness Laboratories
title: Compare a recurrence with an independent state-space search
adaptationNote: The unchanged shared course_test.hpp from Book II B02-L0110 is placed first; the local include is removed. CHECK stays active in optimized builds.

guide.problem: Make structure and path guarantees observable.
guide.design: Collision histories, record identities, graph witnesses, and independent reference solvers expose errors that one answer check misses.
guide.invariant: Every returned witness explains the answer; record identity and key reachability are preserved.
guide.failure: Copying the production recurrence into the oracle repeats the same bug. Testing random hashes may miss collision handling.
guide.trace: Delete one forced-collision key, then search another key that lies beyond its slot.
guide.maintenance: Prefer small adversarial fixtures plus independent oracles to large opaque random tests.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.

experiment: Predict one boundary or tie case, then change this listing and trace the affected state. Delete one forced-collision key, then search another key that lies beyond its slot.

checks.label: Original behavior
checks.hint: Compare the first changed output, assertion, or process exit. Preserve the stated invariant before changing the expected result.
